security_audit.summary: Most static shell execution alerts are Markdown formatting false positives. The audit confirms a critical curl-to-sh installer pattern and a broad unauthenticated authorization example that need remediation.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-sh installation with a pinned release, checksum verification, or package-manager instructions that users can inspect before execution.
Prefer meshTLS identities for ingress clients. If unauthenticated ingress is required, use narrow CIDRs and label all values as placeholders.

remediation.issue: Cluster-changing command examples lack review steps
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run, manifest review, and rollback guidance before examples that pipe generated manifests into kubectl apply.

content.value_statement: Kubernetes teams need repeatable Linkerd patterns for secure service communication and traffic management. This skill provides templates, commands, and checks for Linkerd setup, policy, routing, and observability.
actual_capabilities: Explains core Linkerd architecture and control plane components.
Provides installation, injection, and verification command sequences.
Provides ServiceProfile examples for route metrics, retries, timeouts, and retry budgets.
Shows TrafficSplit and HTTPRoute patterns for canary and version routing.
Provides Server and ServerAuthorization templates for mesh access policy.
Lists monitoring and debugging commands for Linkerd Viz and proxy checks.
limitations: Does not validate commands against a live Kubernetes cluster.
Uses example names, namespaces, URLs, and CIDRs that must be replaced.
Does not choose Linkerd versions or compatibility constraints automatically.
May require additional hardening for regulated or high-risk environments.

use_cases.title: Deploy a Linkerd baseline
use_cases.description: Plan installation, namespace injection, and validation steps for a Kubernetes service mesh rollout.

use_cases.title: Tune service traffic behavior
use_cases.description: Design retries, timeouts, canary traffic splits, and route-level metrics for application services.

use_cases.title: Review mesh access controls
use_cases.description: Draft Server and ServerAuthorization policies that align with service identity and ingress requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Linkerd installation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Linkerd installation for my Kubernetes cluster. Include prerequisites, validation checks, namespace injection, and post-install verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add service mesh injection
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to enable Linkerd injection for this namespace or workload. Include rollout checks and a safe rollback path.

prompt_templates.title: Design traffic policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Linkerd traffic policy for this service. Include route metrics, retry budgets, timeouts, and canary routing guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review zero-trust mesh policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Linkerd authorization plan for zero-trust risk. Identify overly broad access, missing service identities, and safer policy alternatives.

output_examples.input: Plan Linkerd for a new payments namespace.
output: Prerequisites and cluster checks are listed first.
Namespace injection is planned with rollout verification.
Post-install checks cover proxy health, mTLS status, and metrics visibility.

output_examples.input: Create a canary rollout approach for an API service.
output: The response separates stable and canary backends.
It recommends gradual traffic weights and rollback thresholds.
It includes monitoring points for success rate, latency, and retries.

output_examples.input: Review a Linkerd authorization policy for ingress traffic.
output: The response flags broad unauthenticated access.
It suggests meshTLS identities where possible.
It recommends narrow network sources when unauthenticated ingress is unavoidable.

best_practices: Run Linkerd pre-checks and post-install checks before changing production workloads.
Replace every placeholder namespace, service name, URL, and CIDR before applying examples.
Review generated manifests and security policies before applying them to a cluster.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers directly into a shell.
Do not allow unauthenticated access from broad network ranges.
Do not copy example traffic policies without service-specific retry and timeout limits.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps plan and describe Linkerd service mesh setup, traffic policy, authorization, monitoring, and debugging patterns.

faq.question: Can it install Linkerd for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance and templates, but users must review and run commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Does it cover security policy?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Linkerd Server and ServerAuthorization examples, with review needed before production use.

faq.question: Does it support multicluster setups?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes multicluster command patterns and service export checks that must be customized per cluster.

faq.question: What should I customize before use?
faq.answer: Customize namespaces, service names, hostnames, cluster addresses, CIDRs, retry settings, and authorization identities.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
